8. But the principal defendant Nos. 1- 21 have raised claims to the suit land as the successors-in-interest of some persons in whose names SA Khatian No. 51 has been wrongly prepared. Hence the suit. 

 13. On the death of Abdul Alim, his 4 sons, being defendant Nos. 11-14, and another son Renu Bhuyian and two daughters inherited the 1st Suit plot. Upon amicable partition among the said heirs of Abdul Alim (son of Abdul Karim), defendant No. 13 got the entire 1st suit plot and he is in possession thereof. The latest BS Khatian No. 280 has been accordingly prepared in the name of defendant No. 13. 

 20. The said equal shares of the four sons of Abdul Majid have been correctly recorded in the four separate BS Khatians being Nos. 98, 50, 270 and 42 in the names of the defendants and they are in possession thereof. 

 35. Mr Masud next submits that the other documents namely the RS Katian and the latest BS Khatians show that the predecessor of the contesting defendants, after acquisition of the suit land by virtue of the said transfer deed, were in possession and accordingly these records of right were prepared in their names and they have been paying rent. 

 40. The pleadings of the parties show that the contesting defendants admit that the suit land originally belonged to Khorrom Hajee. This is further proved by the two CS Khatians, Exhibit-1 and Exhibit-1 (ka). The CS khatians show that the entire 1st suit plot and the eight anas of share in the suit holding including 2nd suit plot (340) were recorded in the name of Khorrom Hajee. Exhibit-1 (ka) further shows that the entire 2nd suit plot measuring 1.44 acres was possessed by Khorrom Hajee. 

 43. With regard to the time of death of Khorrorn Hajee and the events thereafter, not much evidence is available on record. However, SA Khatian No. 51, Exhibit- 2(kha), shows that the various plots of the earlier CS Khatian No.46, including the 2nd suit plot (CS 340) measuring 1.44 acres were recorded in the names of a number of persons. The name of Khorrom Hajee is not there in the said SA Khatian. Four of those SA recorded tenants are Mohor Chan, daughter of Khorrom Hajee and Abdul Alim, Sahidul Islam, and Idrish Ali, being the three sons of Abdul Majid i.e. the brother of Khorrom Hajee. So the SA Khatian indicates that CS tenant Khorrom died before preparation of the SA Khatian and that there was an amicable partition among the heirs of Khorrom Hajee and the 2nd suit plot, which was in possession of Khorrom Hajee as per CS record, fell in the share of the Mohor Chan. 

 44. The said SA Khatian further proves the truth of the purchase and possession of some land by the three sons of Abdul Majid. It is noted that the 2nd set of defendants claim that the said three sons of Abdul Majid were misled to purchase 51.5 decimals by kabala dated 9-4-1956 (Exhibit-ka) executed by the self declared owner Mohammad Ali, the son of Mohor Chan and father of the plaintiffs. 

 58. The fact of passing of the title to Abdul Majid by virtue of the transfer document of 1957 is further evidenced by the collateral documents, namely the 4 (four) (Halkhatian) (Exhibit-Ga series) prepared in the names of the defendants and also by the rent receipts (Exhibit-Gha series) showing payment of rent by them for the years 1392 to 1412 BS. 

 59. On the possession aspect, the oral evidence adduced by the plaintiffs and the 2nd set of contesting defendants through PWs 1-3 and DWs 1-4 respectively appear to be evenly balanced. But considered with the title documents, Exhibit-Ka and Kha, read with the SA khatian (Exhibit-2), the BS khatians Exhibit- (Ga-series) and the rent receipts, (Exhibits Gha-series), we hold that the testimony of the DWs are credible and that the said defendants are in possession of the 2nd suit plot. 

 62. In respect of the said 1st suit plot, defendant No. 13 or the plaintiffs did not produce the SA Khatian or the certified copy of the BS Khatian or any rent receipt. 

 63. However, defendant No. 13 himself deposed as DW 2 and supported his claim. He also produced a copy of BS Khatian No.280 (Exhibit-A) comprising the single BS plot No. 569 measuring 35 decimals. This document contains the remark of the Union Revenue Assistant “রাজস্ব আদায়ের স্বার্থে বি এস খতিয়ানের অবিকল নকল কপি দেওয়া গেল।” This document is not the certified copy. But it contains the names of defendant No. 13 and his three brothers. 

 64. This document (Exhibit-A) read with our findings on the fact of inheritance of 1/3 share from Khorrom Hajee by his two brothers named Abdul Majid, the predecessor of 2nd set of defendants, Abdul Karim, grandfather of defendant Nos. 11-14, and the fact of inheritance of 2/3 share by the six daughters of Khorrom Hajee, and the admitted amicable partition among those heirs, and the corroborating fact of inclusion of the name of only Mohor Chan as the SA recorded tenant for the only 2nd suit plot and the failure of the plaintiffs to produce any SA Khatian in respect of the 1st suit plot and failure of the plaintiff to prove their possession over the 2nd suit plot, we hold that plaintiffs have failed to prove their exclusive title to, and possession over the 1st suit plot.
